read: not reachable (the news page returns 404 'Article not found'; no excavation report was found)
what_they_did: According to a search-result snippet only, the report describes a circular softstone seal with Indus signs and a humped bull from Umm al-Quwain, dated to about 2300 BCE.
No primary excavation report was found, so the method of dating and reading is unknown.
what_they_found: Nothing could be read from the source itself.
The project's earlier note found that Majchrzak and Degli Esposti 2024 (PAM 33) describes a different seal, TAD.0105, so the two should not be merged (experiments/uaq_seal).
strength_and_limits: A single news item with a dead link is not evidence; the seal's text, shape and context need a primary publication.
Round softstone seals with a bull fit the known Gulf seal type, so the find is plausible but not yet usable.

ideas_for_us.idea: Keep a watch entry and, when a primary report appears, add the seal's sign string to the foreign-seal set and score it under the core-trained grammar model alongside the other Gulf seals.
ideas_for_us.why: One more Gulf seal with a clear text adds to the small set behind our Gulf penalty result.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: A published photograph or drawing with a sign reading.

ideas_for_us.idea: Before adding any new Gulf seal, fix in advance the test it will enter: the bits-per-sign penalty under the core model, compared with the existing Gulf set and with SIGIL outpost texts.
ideas_for_us.why: Pre-registering the test stops a single striking find from being read after the fact.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: The existing foreign-seal set and grammar model.
